general.q: Which is the only Canadian province that is officially bilingual across both English and French?
general.why: New Brunswick adopted official bilingualism in 1969; Quebec's sole official provincial language is French.

general.q: Which is the only non-metallic element that is a liquid at standard room temperature and pressure?
general.why: While mercury is a liquid metal, bromine is the only non-metal to exist in a liquid state at room temperature.

general.q: In South African winemaking, what is the traditional local name for the Chenin Blanc grape?
general.why: Dutch settlers introduced the grape in the 17th century, where it became widely cultivated under the name Steen.

general.q: Which Roman emperor was captured alive by the Sasanian Persian Empire at the Battle of Edessa in 260 AD?
general.why: Valerian became the only Roman emperor to be taken as a prisoner of war, spending the rest of his life in captivity.

general.q: Which is the only bone in the human body that does not articulate directly with any other bone?
general.why: Anchored only by muscles and ligaments in the throat, the hyoid plays an essential role in speech and swallowing.

pop.q: Which rotten borough does Baldrick win by a landslide in Blackadder the Third?
pop.why: Baldrick famously polled one vote (his own) to become MP for Dunny-on-the-Wold.

pop.q: Before being redesigned as British adventurer Lara Croft, what was the character originally named?
pop.why: Core Design swapped the South American mercenary Laura Cruz for an English aristocrat.

pop.q: In 1999, which US intelligence agency banned Furby toys from its premises over fears they could record secrets?
pop.why: The NSA feared the talkative toys had built-in microphones that could repeat classified audio.

pop.q: Which video game are Shaun and Ed playing together in the living room in Shaun of the Dead?
pop.why: Ed is repeatedly seen glued to the PS2 shooter TimeSplitters 2 in their North London flat.

pop.q: Which British musician provided backing vocals on the iconic 1970s 'Secret Lemonade Drinker' advert?
pop.why: Elvis Costello (Declan MacManus) sang uncredited backing vocals on his father Ross's jingle.

music.q: Which song ended Bryan Adams' record-breaking 16-week run at the top of the UK Singles Chart in 1991?
music.why: U2's 'The Fly' knocked 'Everything I Do' from number one in November 1991, spending a single week at the top.

music.q: Which UK town or city hosted the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest, where ABBA took victory with 'Waterloo'?
music.why: Brighton Dome hosted the 1974 contest after 1973 winners Luxembourg declined to stage it again on financial grounds.

music.q: Before co-founding The Police in 1977, which progressive rock band did drummer Stewart Copeland play in?
music.why: Copeland joined Curved Air in 1975 and played on two studio albums before forming The Police with Sting.

music.q: Which synth-pop duo kept 'Fairytale of New York' off the UK Christmas number one spot in 1987?
music.why: Pet Shop Boys topped the 1987 Christmas chart with their cover version of 'Always on My Mind'.

music.q: Which synthesizer, launched in 1983, became the first commercially successful digital FM keyboard?
music.why: The Yamaha DX7 sold over 200,000 units and defined the bright digital synthesizer sound of 1980s pop.

mix.q: Which chemical element derives its name from the Ancient Greek word for 'pale green'?
mix.why: Chlorine comes from 'chloros', referring to the pale yellow-green colour of the gas.

mix.q: In the sitcom Fawlty Towers, in which Spanish city was the waiter Manuel born?
mix.why: Manuel famously repeats that he is 'from Barcelona' throughout the classic series.

mix.q: Which Manchester band had a UK top five hit in 1990 with the single Step On?
mix.why: Happy Mondays scored a massive hit with their reimagined cover of John Kongos's Step On.

mix.q: Which river is responsible for carving out the Grand Canyon in Arizona?
mix.why: The Colorado River has eroded the Grand Canyon over millions of years.

mix.q: Which was the first animated film to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture?
mix.why: Beauty and the Beast was nominated for Best Picture in 1992, before an animated category existed.

mix.q: Which keyboard instrument produces the distinctive flute sounds on the intro to Strawberry Fields Forever?
mix.why: Paul McCartney played the tape-based Mellotron keyboard to create the iconic opening flute sounds.

mix.q: Who was the reigning monarch during the Great Fire of London in 1666?
mix.why: King Charles II personally inspected the firefighting efforts during the four-day blaze.

mix.q: In George Orwell's allegorical novella Animal Farm, what type of animal is Boxer?
mix.why: Boxer is the loyal and hard-working cart-horse whose motto is 'I will work harder'.

mix.q: Which iconic 1973 album features cover art designed by Hipgnosis depicting a prism refracting light?
a: The Dark Side of the Moon
mix.why: Hipgnosis created the famous prism artwork for Pink Floyd's landmark 1973 album.

mix.q: What is the SI unit of electrical conductance, named after a German inventor and industrialist?
mix.why: Siemens (symbol S) is the unit of electric conductance, equal to the reciprocal of resistance.
